decision: A managed-only append-stable prompt representation plus a request-owned physical-call receipt is the smallest route to useful exact cross-turn anchoring. Extending the raw-row hash alone gives safe but usually unusable fallback. Keep H673 partial until both nonstream and SSE actual-dispatch proofs and full-request budget-once behavior pass.
source_constraints: orchestrator.py:2432,2660 appends current user before normal nonstream/SSE planning; _complete_llm_turn:4120-4127 later appends assistant. _shared_route_plan:4610-4674 currently feeds an ephemeral compressed history to _build_agent_turn_text and Agent.build_prompt. Nonstream history includes the just-persisted user, while SSE prior() removes its text to avoid a second copy. One new canonical renderer must handle both without duplication.

orchestrator.py:_build_agent_turn_text:3795-3848 injects attachments, persona, agent context, frozen living core, project, plugin, recall, runtime and approval outcomes. Agent.build_prompt:853-889 adds skills/RAG before `User said:` and Respond-as/IMPORTANT instructions after the entire user text. This one user string is rebuilt every turn, so last turn's provider-visible string is not a prefix of the next. Dynamic blocks must be recomputed and compared; they cannot be frozen merely to preserve a hash.

Agent.generate_response/_generate_response:921-1090 may clock/model-wrap system, append steering, choose a tool runtime, or send generate/generate_stream. Orchestrator SSE:2855-2940 may replace prompt with a Gemini cache tail or checkpoint prefix after the shared plan. AgentToolRuntime._run_loop:650-665,770-795 constructs guided system, live offered tools and mutable tool messages. A plan-time string does not prove the final physical request.

route_compaction.py:241-290 currently subtracts estimated system/current-prompt/schema overhead from each selected route's input allowance, then passes one shared history budget. ContextCompressor._used currently treats UsageAnchor.prompt_tokens as history cost. Because provider prompt_tokens prices the entire request, a measured count must instead be compared to each route's full input ceiling exactly once. The owner memory.compression_max_tokens is a separate history cap.

Existing committed batch10 ManagedAnchorStore remains per Orchestrator and synchronized. Keep session/agent/backend identity/model/instance/raw-prefix checks and 256-entry eviction. checkpoint.commit_clock does not mutate raw rows; last_n head eviction correctly invalidates.

llm/egress.py:_recorder observes each allowed physical HTTP send after host and data-handling guards, including retries/redirects, while usage_context.py publishes accepted text usage and AgentToolRuntime._report_usage publishes structured usage. H002 turn_usage is an accounting collector, not an H673 request-view receipt; do not infer priced-view equivalence from its final bill aggregate.

proposed_types_and_functions.location: new agents/core/managed_prompt.py, with Agent.build_prompt unmanaged unchanged
proposed_types_and_functions.api: @dataclass(frozen=True) ManagedPrompt: prologue: str; rendered_rows: tuple[str,...]; prompt: str; source_prefix_sha256: str; source_count: int; projection_version: str; append_start: int | None. build_managed_prompt(agent, *, host_blocks, context, rendered_history, current_row, source_rows, tainted) -> ManagedPrompt
proposed_types_and_functions.contract: Factor the existing Agent.build_prompt skills/agent-memory/Howard-RAG and Respond-as/IMPORTANT words into a managed host prologue; keep these host instructions ahead of the transcript. Preserve _build_agent_turn_text's existing block producers and trust wrappers, but place their fresh outputs in that prologue rather than after historical turns. The transcript tail is one canonical render_turn projection of accepted rows, including the current user exactly once; future assistant/user rows append `\n` plus render_turn bytes. Use source rows only to prove origin/ordering, never as a substitute for rendered-byte equality. Current-user content must equal the accepted stored row, otherwise mark unanchorable. No new tool authority, no untrusted text moved into a host instruction position. Keep unmanaged prompt bytes unchanged.

proposed_types_and_functions.api: @dataclass(frozen=True) PricedView: kind: Literal['text','tool']; backend_identity: object; model: str; session_instance: str; system_sha256: str; schema_sha256: str; prompt_prefix_sha256: str | None; prompt_chars: int; message_prefix_sha256: str | None; message_count: int; source_prefix_sha256: str; source_count: int; projection_version: str; stable_for_outer_turn: bool. @dataclass(frozen=True) ContextPressure: source: Literal['measured','estimated']; full_prompt_tokens: int; appended_tokens: int; selected_route: PreparedRoute. match_priced_prefix(anchor, candidate, *, raw_rows) -> ContextPressure | None
proposed_types_and_functions.contract: Store only hashes, sizes, counts and provider token count, never raw prompt contents. For text, hash candidate.prompt[:anchor.prompt_chars] and require it equals the old actual prompt hash; system/schema/backend/model/instance/version/raw source prefix must agree. For tools, hash every previous actual provider-visible message and offered ToolSpec through message_count; candidate must retain them verbatim. Compute an estimate only over appended physical tail, with a small delimiter/message framing allowance. A last tool-loop call containing transient result messages is not stable_for_outer_turn and must not become next-turn outer anchor. No sliding-window/summarized-image/rewind/changed-prologue suffix-overlap heuristic.

proposed_types_and_functions.location: agents/core/llm/usage_context.py plus narrow actual-generation call sites in agents/core/agent.py and agents/core/agent_runtime.py; optionally agents/core/llm/egress.py for physical-send confirmation
proposed_types_and_functions.api: @dataclass(frozen=True) PricedObservation: usage: TokenUsage; view: PricedView; accepted_request_id: int. priced_request_scope(candidate: PricedView, sink: Callable[[PricedObservation], None]) -> context manager; note_physical_dispatch(request) -> None; publish_priced_usage(usage: TokenUsage) -> None
proposed_types_and_functions.contract: A closed request-local scope carries the actual dispatch descriptor, not a mutable instance field or an added provider-wire key. Enter only after route/guard/prepared-budget checks, immediately around backend.generate/generate_stream or generate_tool_turn. Capture post-clock/post-model-system/post-steering text arguments and, for tools, post-profile/guidance/post-approval-outcomes `messages` plus the exact offered `tools` passed to the backend. Egress hook confirms an allowed known generation send; unsupported body transforms, unmatched model, multiple incompatible sends, or an absent owned physical dispatch make this H673 observation unanchorable. Pair the accepted terminal usage with that call before scope close; text stream publishes only after its existing terminal gates and tool runtime uses its existing _report_usage seam. The old observer continues H002/legacy accounting independently, including absent/partial usages. No new backend public signature and no provider-wire metadata.

proposed_types_and_functions.location: agents/core/orchestrator.py:_shared_route_plan, SSE _meter and nonstream meter, plus route_compaction.py:plan_shared
proposed_types_and_functions.api: SharedPlan gains accepted ManagedPrompt per agent and source snapshot; route planning calls build(value) for all agents with the same canonical history projection. RoutePressureQuote per selected agent records full input ceiling = int(.85*route.input_budget), current full-request estimate, and optional exact ContextPressure. stage_shared_history(..., quotes) chooses one bounded history rewrite to satisfy every route; after stage, rebuild each actual candidate and recheck route, clock and final prepared budget before any model call.
proposed_types_and_functions.contract: A matched provider observation contributes `observed_full_prompt_tokens + estimate(appended_physical_tail)` against that agent's full input ceiling. Do not subtract plan_shared's estimated scaffold overhead again. For unmatched views, use the complete current projection estimator and existing overhead/budget checks. Keep memory.compression_max_tokens as an independent history limit. If the pressure is high because only system/schema grew and historical compaction cannot make the final request fit, use existing fixed context refusal; never silently spend a different agent's measurement on a shared summary. The final actual-dispatch receipt may replace the stored anchor only after a valid accepted response, and only if it belongs to that agent/session/route.

precise_call_changes: _shared_route_plan.build(value) currently calls _build_agent_turn_text then Agent.build_prompt; for managed paths only, call the new managed builder and return (prompt, estimated_overhead, enriched_or_opaque_input_binding, uses_tools, ManagedPrompt). Both nonstream Agent.process(prepared) and SSE direct Agent.generate_response must receive the exact accepted prompt from PreparedRoute; any post-plan cache/checkpoint/steering rewrite is checked against the actual dispatch receipt and invalidates old anchor reuse unless proved equivalent.

Do not make Agent.process rebuild a managed prompt from current mutable context. Its existing `prepared.input_text` equality, PreparedRoute.check, and pre/post-residency check_budget remain the admission guards. Candidate text/route/session lifetime must be validated before and after any await as now.

At _run_loop, create the physical descriptor after _guided_system and mark_invocation_outcomes_visible, and immediately before generate_tool_turn. _compact_context may rewrite messages/clock before dispatch; descriptor follows the rewritten committed list. _report_usage pairs that same request on return. A prior in-loop response can cover its exact message prefix on the next iteration, but a fold invalidates it.

For text, create the descriptor after model_system_prompt and prepare_steering_rows have finalized system/prompt, immediately before generate/generate_stream. A Gemini cache binding or a backend-specific system/prompt transform needs an actual-dispatch proof; if unavailable, fallback rather than adapting the planned digest by guess. Accepted stream usage arrives only after a validated terminal response, as existing adapters require.

On H673 match, ContextCompressor must not floor the provider count at an estimate of the already measured raw prefix. The separate image-rewrite change already retains a conservative upper bound; exact descriptor matching must invalidate when the priced image-bearing view is altered, then re-anchor on next response. Avoid changing H002 bill sums or approval/taint envelopes.
required_red_regressions: Real offline MockTransport managed nonstream two-turn and SSE two-turn paths: record actual backend arguments. With stable host blocks and unslid context_window, first request's system/schema/full prompt bytes are an exact prefix of the next, and the current user appears once in each. One provider count below raw estimate remains base; a 28k count above it trips the selected 32k/85% pressure tier with only appended rows estimated.

Adversarial content with forged `[assistant]:` and newline delimiters remains data under existing native/foreign framing; imported foreign row uses render_turn taint; changed attachment/current-user stored text, summary, image stripping, or last_n slide refuses exact reuse. The next eligible response can re-anchor.

Same raw rows with changed persona/clock, skills/RAG, live tool schema/profile, plugin, recall, project/runtime/outcome, or backend/model/instance rejects the old physical view. Final post-CAS persona or cache-tail rewrite cannot publish an anchor for the rejected planned view.

Tool loop two accepted physical turns: observer attaches distinct message/tool descriptors to each usage; last eligible response replaces rather than sums. A transient tool-result message makes the final call ineligible for next outer turn; a truly appended in-loop message may reuse prior measured prefix. Tool-result folding or guardian tool withdrawal invalidates. Partial/zero/failed/retried/cancelled/late observations never publish false exact coverage.

Two agents with different systems/schemas/windows and concurrent sessions: one shared history summary honors every selected route's full limit without using the other agent's anchor or double-charging overhead; unknown provider usage falls back. PreparedRoute.check_budget still refuses actual growth before physical send, and H002 request usage is unchanged.

Default unmanaged prompt output remains byte-for-byte unchanged; managed stream/nonstream produce the same canonical current-user history tail. Gemini cache/checkpoint branches either prove exact actual bytes or invalidate and fall back; no paid calls.

tests: stream/physical backend tests chosen by owner
likely_ownership.coordination: The other batch10 agent currently owns context_compressor.py and test_context_usage_anchor.py. Root must explicitly hand off those paths after its image-repair freeze, and settle whether actual priced-view confirmation belongs to egress.py or call-site provenance before splitting implementation ownership.

limits_and_decisions_for_root: Changing the managed prompt layout is user-visible model behavior even though no API shape changes. The host instruction wording and all existing trust/approval boundaries need independent review, not just token tests.

If a provider path cannot expose or verify the accepted physical request view, its usage may still be counted for H002 but is H673-unanchorable. Do not promote the whole row on one supported backend without stating the coverage boundary.

No provider can tell us the isolated token price of a removed image or a rewritten summary. Invalidation or an explicitly conservative upper bound is the honest policy; exact self-correction resumes after the next accepted response.
The current default memory.context_compression is off. Whole H673 equivalence is about the enabled supported path and selected physical routes, not a claim that default-off sessions compact.
